name: Nurzhan
note: Oil and refining city (Kobozev 1927–92), city of governorate significance on the lower Chu plain; sits on the site of real Shu.

name: Northern Steppe
note: UN planning zone ~119,600 km²: the southern Betpak-Dala north of the Chu, the Moiynkum sands between the Chu and the Talas and the piedmont plain north of the ISEZ belt; Boztorgoy winter pastures.

name: Talas Alatau
note: UN planning zone ~8,100 km²: the north slope and crest of the Talas Alatau above the Talas valley, from Aksu-Zhabagly on the Kazakh frontier east to the State Route 1 corridor: Aksay Plateau, Kara-Koyun, upper Besh-Tash and Kara-Suu, Manas Peak.

name: Kara-Bulak
note: Market town and grain/maize collection point on the valley rail spur, ~35 km west of Talas in the middle valley; Andronovo kurgans; NAI grain depot.

name: Qara-Chik
note: Village at the mouth of the Kara-Buura valley, where the road from Kyzyl-Adyr into the Chatkal valley leaves the plain; the Qara-Chik Border Checkpoint stands just above it, and the ceasefire line is named after it. Called Chong-Kara-Buura on Soviet maps.

name: Ak-Terek
note: Village of white poplars and orchards in the southern foothills of the Talas valley; commuters to Talas.

name: Tegirmen
note: Trout-farming village at the confluence of the Urmaral and the Talas, west of the capital.

name: Sarymsakty
note: Garlic and onion smallholdings in the middle Talas valley east of Talas (formed 1994).

name: Kümüshtü
note: Village in the eastern Talas District, upper Talas valley, beside the medieval silver-mining site of Shelji.

name: Kök-Oi
note: Village at the mouth of the Besh-Tash valley ~20 km south of Talas; Besh-Tash Ranger Headquarters and guesthouses.

name: Sabz-Kand
note: Vineyard village in the foothills east of Talas watered by Kok-Tash kariz galleries.

name: Jangy-Kent
note: Modern village beside the Kara-Khanid mound of Kand-i Nau in the foothills east of Talas, on a kariz branch.

name: Almaluu
note: Apple-orchard and felt-cooperative village in the southern foothills east of the capital.

name: Arsha-Say
note: Village on a side stream of the Talas below the Talas Alatau; birthplace and burial place of the writer Kemel Ishakov.

name: Tash-Bulak
note: Village in the Muz-Suu valley damaged by the 2016 Muz-Köl outburst flood; Muz-Suu placed beside the Urmaral west of the capital (sensors in both valleys).

name: Uuk-Bulak
note: Yurt-frame makers' village in the foothills south-west of Talas.

name: Jangy-Jol
note: 1995 resettlement village for war-displaced families on the southern side of the valley west of the capital.

name: Köpürö-Bazar
note: Village at the road bridge over the Talas west of the capital, near the Central Cattle Mart; wool and hide auctions.

name: Shagyldy
note: Gravel-quarry village on the stony fan of a dry ravine on the northern side of the Talas valley.

name: Teskey-Jar
note: Village on a loess terrace above the gorge of the upper Talas, eastern Talas District (2004 cliff collapse).

name: Toguz-Bulak
note: Roadside village and snowplough depot at the foot of the southern approach to the Kök-Bel Pass (Talas–Chu road).

name: Bakyyan
note: At chabysh horse-training village ~8 km east of Kyzyl-Adyr in the lower Talas valley.

name: Taldy-Suu
note: Willow and honey village on a side channel of the Talas River in the lower valley.

name: Ak-Döbö
note: Village partly on a Bronze Age/medieval settlement mound in the lower Talas valley.

name: Ming-Örük
note: Orchard village on the Kenkol fan where the river leaves the Talas Alatau for the western valley, near Karool-Döbö and the Kenkol burial ground; kept west of Kara-Bulak so it stays in Kara-Buura.

name: Eski-Korgon
note: Village around an 1830s Kokand fort on the old road down the lower Talas valley toward the Kazakh border.

name: Chet-Bulak
note: 1908 Russian settlers' village with a single poplar-lined street on the northern side of the lower Talas valley.

name: Tunuk-Bulak
note: Karst-spring village in the limestone foothills south of Talas (same belt as the Kyrk-Kazyk Caves and Maryam-Bulak).

name: Besh-Terek
note: Sugar-factory village (Chui Sugar Refining Corp.) in the irrigated lowlands west of Nurzhan.

name: Shahr-i Nav
note: Grid-plan 1960s state-farm village on the Jangy-Aryk branch canal north of Nurzhan.

name: Besh-Moinok
note: Melon village at the tail of a branch canal on the northern edge of the irrigated land NW of Nurzhan, where farmland meets the Moiynkum sands.

name: Jon-Aryk
note: Koryo-saram rice village founded 1937–38 on the lower Chu south-west of Nurzhan.

name: Shaar-Döbö
note: Village ~30 km west of Nurzhan beside the Sogdian/Kara-Khanid site of Shahr-i Buzurg.

name: Kum-Aryk
note: Greenhouse village on the eastern outskirts of Nurzhan near the oil fields (gas flaring).

name: Sary-Döbö
note: Village (ex-Zheltaya Mogila, 1891) around the ruined fort of Diz-i Zard in the lower Chu valley; placed downstream (NW) of Nurzhan. (Moved onto the real road in Oct 2026.)

name: Temirchi
note: Blacksmiths' village ~15 km north of Nurzhan.

name: Kök-Döbö
note: Village on a low hill on the southern side of the Chu lowlands SE of Nurzhan; weather radar on the summit.

name: Aral
note: Village on a strip of land between two channels of the Chu west of Nurzhan.

name: Uch-Emchek
note: Sugar-beet village beside three hillocks west of Nurzhan, supplying the Besh-Terek factory.

name: Tash-Kömür
note: Coal-mining town on the Naryn at ~600 m where it leaves the mountains; seat of Lower Naryn District, UNMI sector HQ, south end of State Route 1 (236 km from Talas).

name: Kapka-Tash
note: Village below Tash-Kömür on the road toward the Uzbek border at the mouth of a short side gorge of the Naryn.

name: Jyluu-Bulak
note: Spa village with 42 °C sulfur springs in a side valley of the Naryn above Tash-Kömür.

name: Bulak-Bashy
note: 1965 dam-builders' village on the Naryn above Tash-Kömür; hydropower and switchyard workers.

name: Altyn-Bulak
note: Mineral-water bottling village in the foothills north of Tash-Kömür.

name: Chong-Kapka
note: Chongtor-breeding winter village on Tanıp pastures in the upper Kara-Suu valley, just above the rock gateway where the river leaves its upper valley (head of the Kara-Suu Canyon).

name: Kara-Koyun
note: Karakoyun clan winter gathering place in the Kara-Koyun Valley south of Kara-Buura District near the line; stone pens and winter houses; extraordinary Kurultai venue.

name: Kashka-Jol
note: Pack-horse hamlet in the middle Kara-Buura valley on the old route over the Kara-Buura Pass to the Chatkal.

name: Kyrk-Bulak
note: Spring-line village in the limestone foothills of the western Talas Alatau, south of Kara-Buura District; Chongtor breeders.

name: Kyrk-Choro
note: Village in a valley below the northern face of Manas Peak at the western end of the range; manaschy gathering each August.

name: Orto-Ayyl
note: Upper Talas valley village just beyond the Qara-Chik line; council of elders under adat since 2008.

name: Kara-Kungey
note: Apple and potato village on the sunny side of a valley in the northern Talas Alatau.

name: Kosh-Döbö
note: Seasonal herders' camps (~400 people, June–September) at ~2,460 m below the Aksay Plateau, about 6 km from the Kurultai ground.

name: Kanysh-Kiya
note: Largest village of the Chatkal valley: secondary school, hospital, weekly market, gold washing (approximate real location). (Moved onto the real river in Oct 2026.)

name: Kyzyl-Bel
note: Sheep and yak hamlet in the upper Chatkal valley at the foot of the Kyzyl-Bel Pass (2,450 m).

name: Teke-Tash
note: Village at ~2,550 m on the southern slopes of the Talas Alatau above the Chatkal valley, at the upper limit of spruce.

name: Archaly
note: Village in a forested side valley of the Chatkal (spruce and juniper).

name: Jashyl-Köl
note: Summer yurt settlement of ~25 families at ~1,530 m in the valley below Jashyl-Köl (the moraine lake at ~2,600 m) on the southern slopes of the Chatkal range, on the route to Sary-Chelek.

name: Besh-Köl
note: Summer herders' camp (8–10 families) at ~2,860 m below five glacial lakes in the upper Chatkal range.

name: Ozgörüsh
note: 1974–75 resettlement village on the lower Uzun-Akmat above the reservoir; Uzun-Akmat Terraces; Kökjal clan elder's home (approximate location).

name: Kara-Jylga
note: Remote village at the head of a side valley north of the reservoir, 24 km dirt track (cut off by avalanches 2012, 2026).

name: Tash-Köröö
note: Cobble-built goat-herding village in a side valley above the reservoir, below a box canyon used as a pen.

name: Kara-Say
note: Barley-terrace village at ~1,900 m in the Fergana Range foothills above the Toktogul basin.

name: Kosh-Bel
note: Hamlet (~150 people) at ~2,400 m on the migration route from the Toktogul basin to the Fergana Range pastures; veterinary post.

name: Arslanbob
note: Walnut-forest village at ~1,600 m in the upper Kara-Unkur valley ~40 km NE of Bazar-Korgon; Arslanbob-Ata shrine, waterfalls, guesthouses.

name: Kyzyl-Unkur
note: Village in the Kara-Unkur valley named in the Oct 2026 tremor report (epicentre a few km NE); a real village of this name exists, but it is placed here between Bazar-Korgon and Arslanbob to match the report.

name: Sopol-Tepa
note: Uzbek-speaking potters' village near Bazar-Korgon by the Chopo-Jar clay bluffs.

name: Örüktü
note: Terraced apricot village on the northern rim of the Fergana Valley.

name: Kara-Jygach
note: Walnut-harvest village at the lower edge of the walnut-fruit forest on the southern slopes of the Chatkal range above the Fergana Valley.

name: Jangak-Bulak
note: Village at ~1,900 m inside the walnut-fruit forest on the southern slopes of the Fergana Range west of Arslanbob; its sacred walnut grove is about 2 km below.

name: Bazar-Terek
note: Thursday wool and sheep market in the Karatau foothills where tracks from the Kyzylkum Fringe winter pastures meet the road to the Talas valley.

name: Hauzdy
note: Hamlet beside the ruined caravanserai of Rabat-i Kamal on the old road along the Karatau foothills west of the Talas valley.

name: Tar-Say
note: Red-clay hamlet at the mouth of a Kök-Moinok canyon in the Karatau foothills (2016 flash flood).

name: Kyzyl-Döbö
note: Saddlers' village at the foot of red sandstone cliffs in the Karatau foothills; sells at Bazar-Terek.

name: Bitik-Tash
note: Petroglyph village in the Karatau foothills.

name: Tuzduu
note: Brackish-well camel and sheep village on the edge of the Kulan-Talaa plain in western Irad.

name: Sasyk-Bulak
note: Village at the foot of the Karakyr Range on the western edge of Irad; raptor-count base.

name: Ak-Jar
note: Karakul-sheep village under a limestone escarpment near the Kazakh border on the semi-desert western edge.

name: Tört-Kuduk
note: 1964 hydrogeological-expedition village on the southern edge of the Betpak-Dala; supply point for the Keng-Talaa pastures.

name: Ak-Jal
note: Horse-herding village on the southern edge of the Betpak-Dala near the Keng-Talaa race course.

name: Kaiyrma
note: Reed-cutting and fishing village on the lower Chu below the irrigated zone. (Moved onto the real river in Oct 2026.)

name: Kamyshtuu
note: Reed and muskrat hamlet beside drainage marshes on the northern edge of the irrigated Chu lowlands, at the edge of the sands.

name: Ak-Chiy
note: Chiy-screen weaving village on the salt flats of the southern margin of the Moiynkum sands.

name: Töö-Kuduk
note: Camel-herding hamlet at a well in the western Moiynkum sands.

name: Kyrgyz Range–Suusamyr
note: UN planning zone ~4,100 km²: the high Kyrgyz Range pastures east of the Kök-Bel road (since 2009) and the Suusamyr side east of the State Route 1 corridor: Toguz-Bulak, Otmek, the Western Karakol valley, Ak-Kyya.
